hypothesis: A large fraction of teacher-weight residual catastrophic deformation is caused by fused cross-mechanical-region topology. Splitting mixed-region triangles in place with duplicated seam vertices can remove that mechanical coupling without deleting rest geometry.

oracle_boundary.region_labels: Teacher source connected-component labels are diagnostic oracle only.
oracle_boundary.weights: Teacher weights are held fixed as weight oracle so topology is the only causal variable.

held_fixed: original rest positions for existing vertices
original triangle geometric domain; subdivision may add midpoint/centroid vertices only
teacher weight authority for existing vertices
intervention: No original face area may be deleted.
Mixed-region triangles are subdivided into region-pure subtriangles.
Seam vertices are duplicated per region at identical rest positions.
New seam weights are derived only from same-region endpoints/face vertices for this oracle test.

causal_effect_requirements: synthetic unsafe-face count reduced by at least 65% relative to 1553
actual-motion max edge>10 count reduced by at least 65% relative to 592
actual-motion worst edge ratio reduced by at least 50% relative to 118.61562382457814
preregistered_success.interpretation: If all hard requirements and at least two of three causal-effect requirements pass, holeless topological split is a viable repair architecture for the cross-region failure class. It is not yet a teacher-free product operator.

failure_interpretation: Do not promote split/remesh architecture solely from visual coverage. If mechanics do not improve under fixed teacher weights, continue topology owner search.
